question: Do finite, connected, read-twice, irredundant, locally lawful not-all-equal presentations with equal words have identical holdings unless closed? Which marginal order recovers the words? Compare parity.
primary_observable: All ten-name whole-state classes, alternative physical covers, closure and parent rosters. Structured recovery proofs; order-p full and support-only tables. Fresh initial and funded first-stage certified recovery shares for two laws in three panels.
forbidden_inputs: Do not infer actual holding ambiguity from failure of a sufficient recovery test; do not infer different births from different closed holdings, or probability tables from projection support. No identification via independent bit flips of names.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Six-name closed alternate ternaries, earliest five-name parity birth difference, and eight-name quartets that lose named word information at order two.
first_executable_signal: Regrade all width-ten presentations and compare every relation left undecided by the established mandatory-candidate reader.
resource_budget: Six GiB per process, complete width ten, fresh 128 draws per weighting, 256 births at most for each one-step sampled check. Register any check expected to exceed ten minutes.
stop_rule: All five ordered parts; settle the universal question by proof, smallest genuinely different births, or complete ten-distinction exhaustion with the largest proved class.
decision_or_followup_rule: Distinguish model versus supplied growth law, fixed start, supplied weighting and marginal reading, with independent referee pending; report separately to A97 and A128.
